questions.question: Was Mc Donald's Azerbaijan official account posting about military stuff

statements.statement: The official Instagram account of McDonald’s in Azerbaijan posted patriotic photos that appeared to endorse the ongoing combat in Nagorno-Karabakh, including one specific post showing the Azerbaijani flag over a mountain with the text 'Karabakh is Azerbaijan!' and a caption stating 'Let our flag fly over all our native soil of Azerbaijan!'
statements.support_span: Social media users on Twitter were surprised on Oct. 27 to see the official Instagram account of McDonald’s in Azerbaijan posting patriotic photos that appeared to endorse the ongoing combat in Nagorno-Karabakh | One such post displayed the flag of Azerbaijan flying over a mountain vista with the proclamation, “Karabakh is Azerbaijan!” A caption on the photo read, “Let our flag fly over all our native soil of Azerbaijan!”

statements.statement: The McDonald’s Corporation confirmed that their franchisee in Azerbaijan removed the social media content in question, and by October 28, 2020, the McDonald’s Instagram account in Azerbaijan had been taken down.
statements.support_span: “Our franchisee in Azerbaijan has removed the social media content,” the McDonald’s Corporation confirmed to Polygraph.info. | By October 28, both the Azerbaijani Burger King and McDonald’s accounts had been taken down from Instagram.

statements.statement: The Armenian National Committee of America called for a boycott of McDonald’s due to the posts.
statements.support_span: Separately, the group Armenian National Committee of America issued a statement calling for a boycott of McDonald’s until the company takes action on the matter.

silver.justification: The evidence indicates that the official Instagram account for McDonald’s in Azerbaijan posted patriotic content, including an image of the Azerbaijani flag with the text 'Karabakh is Azerbaijan!' and a caption supporting the reclamation of native soil, which appeared to endorse the combat in Nagorno-Karabakh. Following public reaction and a boycott call from the Armenian National Committee of America, McDonald’s Corporation confirmed that the franchisee removed the content, and the account was subsequently taken down by October 28, 2020.
